description: is compares like == with a string in either quote or a bare word that names no variable
code:
value = "EXACT"
[(value is "EXACT"), (value is 'EXACT'), (value is EXACT), (value is not EXACT)]

description: A bare word after is reads the variable of that name once one is defined
code:
code = "A1"
flag = (code is A1)
A1 = "B2"
[flag, (code is "A1")]

description: Deleting the variable returns a bare word to its own text and re-evaluates the comparison
code:
mode = "AUTO"
AUTO = "MANUAL"
auto = (mode is AUTO)
delete AUTO
auto

description: A standing if rule with is follows its subject
code:
status = "PENDING"
if status is SHIPPED:
    stage = "done"
else:
    stage = "open"
status = "SHIPPED"
stage

description: is matches numbers, booleans and property reads with the loose equality of ==
code:
order = {total: 30, paid: true, status: "OPEN"}
[(order.total is 30), (order.total is "30"), (order.paid is true), (order.status is not CLOSED)]

description: A class-level rule compares each instance property with a bare word
code:
class Ticket(state):
    this.state = state
$Ticket.closed = ($Ticket.state is CLOSED)
a = Ticket("CLOSED")
b = Ticket("OPEN")
[a.closed, b.closed]

description: Arrow and lambda callbacks take is and is not
code:
colors = ["RED", "BLUE", "RED"]
reds = colors.filter(c => c is RED)
others = colors.filter(lambda c: c is not RED)
[reds.length, others]

description: Where a statement can follow, is stays a name, so an assigned comparison is parenthesized
code:
is = "name"
value = 1
plain = value is 2
wrapped = (value is 1)
[plain, wrapped, is]

description: A bare word that names a built-in is read as that built-in, so quote it to compare text
